title: Net Asset Classification
description: Understand net assets with donor restrictions and net assets without donor restrictions.
html:
The Two Net Asset Classes

Not-for-profit organizations report net assets in two broad classes based primarily on whether donor-imposed restrictions exist.

Without Donor Restrictions No Donor-Imposed Restriction
With Donor Restrictions Donor-Imposed Restriction Exists

Without Donor Restrictions

Net assets without donor restrictions generally include resources that are not subject to donor-imposed restrictions.

Example

A donor contributes $50,000 and tells the organization to use the money wherever it is most needed.

$50,000 → WITHOUT DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Board Designations

An organization's governing board may decide to designate resources for a particular purpose.

A board designation is an internal decision, not a donor-imposed restriction.

BOARD DESIGNATION ≠ DONOR RESTRICTION
Example

The board designates $100,000 of otherwise unrestricted resources for a future building project.

The amount generally remains within net assets without donor restrictions.

With Donor Restrictions

Resources are generally classified as with donor restrictions when a donor imposes a restriction on their use or timing.

Purpose Restriction

A donor may require that contributed resources be used for a specific program or activity.

Example

A donor contributes $80,000 specifically for a scholarship program.

SPECIFIC DONOR PURPOSE → WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Time Restriction

A donor may specify that resources cannot be used until a future period.

Example

A donor contributes $60,000 in December and requires that the organization use the contribution during the following year.

The contribution is subject to a donor-imposed time restriction.

Restrictions That Do Not Expire Through Spending

Some donor restrictions require contributed resources to be maintained according to the donor's instructions.

A common example is a donor-restricted endowment in which the original gift must generally be maintained subject to the donor's stipulations.

DONOR-RESTRICTED ENDOWMENT → NET ASSETS WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Release From Restriction

A donor restriction may be satisfied when the required purpose is accomplished or the required time period passes.

When that happens, the organization generally reports a release from donor restrictions.

RESTRICTION SATISFIED → RELEASE FROM RESTRICTION → WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS DECREASES WITHOUT DONOR RESTRICTIONS INCREASES

Example — Purpose Restriction Released

A donor previously contributed $90,000 specifically for educational programs.

During the current year, the organization incurs $90,000 of qualifying educational program costs and satisfies the donor restriction.

Net Assets With Donor Restrictions − $90,000
Net Assets Without Donor Restrictions + $90,000

The release changes the classification of net assets; it does not create a second contribution.

The Donor Controls the Classification

Management intentions alone generally do not create donor restrictions.

The key question is whether the restriction came from the donor.

ASK: WHO CREATED THE RESTRICTION? DONOR → WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS BOARD / MANAGEMENT → GENERALLY WITHOUT DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Quick Classification Practice

Donor: "Use this for cancer research." WITH RESTRICTIONS
Donor: "Use this however you need." WITHOUT RESTRICTIONS
Board reserves money for a building. WITHOUT RESTRICTIONS
Donor: "Do not use until next year." WITH RESTRICTIONS

CPA Memory Rule

DONOR SAYS WHEN / WHY → WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS ORGANIZATION DECIDES WHEN / WHY → WITHOUT DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Key Takeaways

  • NFP net assets have two broad classes.
  • Donor-imposed purpose and time restrictions generally create net assets with donor restrictions.
  • Board designations generally do not create donor-restricted net assets.
  • Satisfying a donor restriction may result in a release from restriction.
  • Always identify who imposed the restriction.

quiz.prompt: A not-for-profit organization's board designates $200,000 of unrestricted resources for construction of a future headquarters. No donor imposed this restriction. How should the $200,000 generally be classified?
quiz.explanation: A board designation is an internal restriction rather than a donor-imposed restriction. Therefore, the resources generally remain classified as net assets without donor restrictions.
